perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective:

- I am Ethan, a plumber. Gary Guo is my close friend since middle school; he is a doctor.
- I noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. I became concerned and invited him to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- I told Gary his health was just as important, that I hated seeing him like this, and suggested a two-day retreat might give him a new perspective. Gary said he appreciated my concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat with Gary, I observed him acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected something more than professional obligations was behind his overwork.
- I confronted him, reminding him we’d been friends since middle school and that he could tell me anything; I was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden me with his problems.
- After that, Gary opened up to me about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. I felt relief and empathy. I suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary said that sounded good and that he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. I saw him making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and encouraged him. He told me things were better, thanks to my help, that he was less overwhelmed, and that he had had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, I saw Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. I felt satisfied and happy for him. I decided to step back, but told him I was always just a call away and that he had this. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and felt more in control.
